result.title: Hybrid Spark: Adaptive Speculative Decoding That Lets the Content Choose the Drafter
result.summary: Speculative decoding (SD) speeds up large language model (LLM) serving, but its gain depends on the workload's \emph{shape}, such as batch size and context length, and on its \emph{content}. A model-based drafter proposes a short block on any content, while a model-free drafter such as n-gram lookup proposes long copies at almost no cost when the output repeats its input, as in code editing. Adaptive verification spends a batch-wide verification budget on the draft tokens most likely to be accepted, but it supports only one model-based drafter. Model-free drafters provide no per-token confidence, so they cannot take part in budget allocation, and deployments must either fix one drafter or split their GPUs between drafters. We present \sys, a framework that runs a model-based and a model-free drafter on every step and gives each request the better of their chains, within adaptive verification and entirely on the GPU, which keeps asynchronous scheduling intact. The key idea is a price per verified draft token: the goodput that slot would earn elsewhere in the batch. Once the model-free drafter's tokens carry calibrated acceptance estimates, fit once on general text, this price puts both drafters' chains on one scale. Instantiated with \dspark and an n-gram drafter in vLLM, \sys achieves 1.10--1.62\x the output throughput of \dspark on code editing at batch size~4 and 1.04--1.27\x at batch size~128, while staying at 0.97--1.01\x of it on chat at temperature~0. A single deployment can therefore serve both workloads.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Hybrid Spark 框架，在每一步同时运行基于模型与无模型的 drafter，并以「每个待验证 draft token 在 batch 其他位置可换得的机会收益」作为统一价格，配合校准后的接受率估计，为每条请求挑选更优的草稿链且保持异步调度。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按 token 估计接受概率并据此分配验证预算、把计算机会成本显式定价的思路，可能为 LVR 中动态计算分配与「STOP」式验证权衡提供可核查线索；但论文本身面向纯文本 LLM 服务吞吐，不涉及视觉或多模态推理状态，迁移可行性需自行判断。
